  Ruling 2 — signing key integrity at boot
    REQUIRE_SIGNING_KEY=true (the production contract, testable outside production)
      [32m✓[39m [2mMISSING key pair → refuses to boot and mints NOTHING (19 ms)[22m
      [32m✓[39m [2mkey PRESENT but not decryptable with the configured passphrase → refuses to boot (the live defect) (247 ms)[22m
      [32m✓[39m [2ma usable key pair → boots and signs (116 ms)[22m
    development / test (generation allowed, but never quietly)
      [32m✓[39m [2mMISSING key pair → generates AND logs a loud dev-key warning (135 ms)[22m
      [32m✓[39m [2mUNUSABLE key pair → refuses rather than overwriting the key that signed old certificates (89 ms)[22m
    SIGNING_KEY_FINGERPRINT guard (wrong key is worse than no key)
      [32m✓[39m [2mmatching fingerprint → boots (114 ms)[22m
      [32m✓[39m [2mmismatched fingerprint → refuses to boot even though the key loads fine (314 ms)[22m
      [32m✓[39m [2mmismatch is fatal in dev too — a generated dev key can never match a pinned fingerprint (190 ms)[22m
      [32m✓[39m [2mfingerprintPublicKey is stable, hex, and tolerant of CRLF checkout (192 ms)[22m
